clue.text: Just bills to settle?

definitions.note: an infinitive phrase, matching the verb phrase of the answer

parts.note: fair and even-handed is square, as in a square deal
invoices are accounts sent to customers

explanation.surface: A fair-minded person sets about paying the invoices that have piled up.
explanation.definitionFit: To square accounts is to pay off what is owed and so clear a debt.

clue.text: Light open carriage of shape not unusual

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a carriage whose shape is quite ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the eight letters of SHAPE NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light two- or four-wheeled horse-drawn gig with no hood, named after a clergyman who first had one built.

clue.text: Socially acceptable, paid tribute and exalted

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, socially correct usage
to have paid tribute is to have praised

explanation.surface: A respectable figure is honoured and raised to a lofty position.
explanation.walkthrough: U (upper-class, as opposed to non-U) is a crossword convention for socially acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exalted has been lifted high, and the answer means raised upwards.

clue.text: Bring up the end

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring up the end of a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise children is to bring them up; the back or tail of something is also called this word.

clue.text: See 1
Clearly nothing missing on the inventory

definitions.text: Clearly nothing missing on the inventory

parts.words: Clearly nothing missing on the inventory
parts.note: a register of items that leaves nothing out describes itself as whole and full

explanation.surface: A stocktaker reports that every item is accounted for.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory with nothing missing is an entire catalogue, every item included.

clue.text: Bits of a sort topped and tailed

indicators.note: the top letter of the word sort is taken off and put on as its tail

explanation.surface: Scraps of some kind have had their ends trimmed off, like vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' usually means both ends removed; here the top letter S moves to the tail, making ORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are leftover scraps of food, odds and ends.

clue.text: Ornamental work Lionel designs

indicators.note: as a verb, designs means works out a new arrangement, so the name's letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A craftsman named Lionel creates decorative pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic inlay used to decorate engraved silver.

clue.text: Seems a variety of aromatic plant

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so these letters take another arrangement

explanation.surface: Something appears to be a kind of fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a herbaceous plant grown for its oily, nutty-scented seeds.

clue.text: Line of flight

parts.note: a route that aircraft follow, like a shipping lane in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: An airway is a designated corridor through which aircraft travel.

clue.text: Parent on board takes one's breath away

indicators.note: on, in the sense of aboard a vessel, puts one piece inside the ship's letters

parts.note: board read as a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship
a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A mother on a voyage finds the view stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the crossword habit of putting a word inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother someone is to suffocate them, literally stopping their breathing.

clue.text: Derelict with shivering timbers?

parts.note: a ship abandoned and broken, its timbers trembling as if from anxiety

explanation.surface: A ghostly abandoned hulk creaks in the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose nerves are in tatters is pictured as a shattered, trembling ship.

clue.text: Greet with acclaim

explanation.surface: Welcoming someone with loud praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone on meeting, and to praise someone enthusiastically, as in being hailed a hero.

clue.text: Cathedral city that springs to mind?

explanation.surface: A city with a cathedral is the first that occurs to you.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells is a small city in Somerset, England, with a famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells is an English cathedral city; things that well up in the mind are springing forth like water from the ground.

clue.text: Choice tree

explanation.surface: A pick of the orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice job is a plum one; it is also a fruit tree bearing stone fruit.

clue.text: Part of the intake Babylonians enjoyed?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about what part of ancient Babylonian diets was relished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enjoyed' defines with the question mark: a kebab is something one enjoys eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of grilled meat on skewers is food that people relish eating.

clue.text: Sort of call needing operator in!

definitions.text: Sort of call needing operator in!

indicators.note: in puts the operator's letter inside the word call
sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A phone call that has to be put through by the exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a call within the same area once went through a local operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbourhood phone call, within one's own exchange area, is described by this word.

clue.text: Quiet establishment for safekeeping

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, quiet
a reservation is an area established and set aside

explanation.surface: A tranquil institution where things are held safely.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something safe from harm or decay is its protection.

clue.text: Understandable measure from a recent leading parliamentarian

explanation.surface: A measure brought in by a recent party leader that everyone can grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party 1980-83, so his rule is Foot's rule; 'understandable' hints at what one stands on.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler marked in inches up to twelve is a measuring stick; the government of a politician named Foot would be his rule.

clue.text: Fruit grove in 22, perchance

explanation.surface: Citrus trees growing in a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is ANTRIM, a county of Northern Ireland, where the Protestant Orange Order is strong.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhouse or plantation for citrus trees; also Orange Order loyalism, found in Antrim.

clue.text: Indifferent attitude to work occasionally?

parts.note: a relaxed approach to one's job, or work taken on only now and then

explanation.surface: A worker who only occasionally cares about the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers hired temporarily as needed form a pool of temporary, irregular hands.

clue.text: Frenchman with little brother at school

parts.note: Br is the short form of brother
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A French boy and his younger sibling are pupils at an English school.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Brittany, in north-west France.

clue.text: County worker on edge

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: An employee in a rural area stands on the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Crack right at the finish

parts.note: the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A crack appears on the right-hand side at the close.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear something apart violently is to split it.

clue.text: Smart, it's said, from stroke of the birch

explanation.surface: A sharp stroke of the cane leaves a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for fashionable and elegant; it is also the swishing sound and stroke of a cane through air.

clue.text: Automatic in the best English tradition

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Something done without thought in the finest English way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War, an automatic weapon.

clue.text: Serpentine neckwear

explanation.surface: A snake-like scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: Large constricting snakes, and long feathery scarves; the first sense is the snakes themselves rather than an adjective.

clue.text: Gown cut out in Scutari

indicators.note: out says the word cut is removed from the place name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dress tailored in an Ottoman city.
explanation.walkthrough: Scutari is the old name of Üsküdar in Istanbul, where Florence Nightingale nursed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sari is a long draped garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Pieman's sales incentive?

parts.note: a baker selling pastries cares about the volume of business, and his product is a folded pastry

explanation.surface: A baker looks for ways to sell more pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnover is a business's total sales, and also a folded pastry with a filling.

clue.text: Adult companion touring an ancient city

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a mate is a companion
Ur was the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A grown-up travelling with a friend visits ancient ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully grown and developed, as a grown-up is.

clue.text: Specify Japanese beer or another so called

parts.note: to name something is to specify it
sake is fermented Japanese rice drink, brewed like beer

explanation.surface: Asking a bar to name its Japanese drink or some other brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing sharing the same name as another.

clue.text: Excited Peter the portrait painter about teatime

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was the court portraitist of Charles II
four o'clock is teatime, written in Roman numerals as IV

explanation.surface: A painter gets agitated around afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Teatime is traditionally four o'clock in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of energy and animation, spirited.
